identityReview: Justin Pierre James Trudeau, born Ottawa on 25 December 1971; distinguish father Pierre’s premiership and full name. McGill BA 1994 and UBC BEd 1998, followed by teaching. Papineau MP from 14 October 2008 through 27 April 2025 according to Commons roles; Liberal leadership election 14 April 2013 differs from role commencement 15 April. Canada’s 23rd prime minister from 4 November 2015 until resignation on 14 March 2025. Successor Carney elected party leader 9 March and sworn premier 14 March. No current premiership or parliamentary seat. November 2026 Oxford fellowship is based on the Canadian Press report, not assumed professorial employment.
lifeStatusEvidence: Brown University’s 22 September 2026 report documents Trudeau’s actual on-stage discussion with president Christina Paxson and attributed remarks, identifying him as former prime minister. The Canadian Press’s 7 November report adds a newly announced Oxford role and his quoted response but is not proof of an actual campus visit. The earlier Brown advertisement alone would not establish attendance.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read historical UN biography, UBC alumni paragraph, CNN/KEYT personal and early-career facts, Commons role/election tables and selected appendices, Governor General ceremony records, ethics commissioner release and selected report excerpts, Global Affairs CUSMA introduction and present review-page opening, Reuters minority-election account, Health Canada cannabis release, Finance Canada and CRA fuel-charge notices, Brown’s completed-event report, Canadian Press Oxford appointment story, and Commons/Council rights metadata. Source review is scoped to stated sections, not all linked materials.
corrections: Read the UN Office for Partnerships historical biography: 25 December 1971 birth; McGill BA in 1994; UBC education programme and Vancouver teaching; 2007 party nomination versus 2008 election; 2013 party leadership; 19 October 2015 majority victory and 4 November swearing-in. Its present-tense prime-minister and SDG-co-chair descriptions are dated, not verified current roles. Institutional praise is not an independent impact assessment. The page does not give the UBC graduation year; that is established separately.

Read UBC’s alumni paragraph explicitly identifying Trudeau’s Bachelor of Education in 1998 and calling him a former national leader. This is separate from the 1994 McGill BA. Do not confuse a teaching qualification with a law degree, PhD or the honorary credentials of other alumni on the page. No original diploma was inspected.

Read CNN Editorial Research’s personal facts and selected early timeline, syndicated by KEYT: Ottawa birth on 25 December 1971, full name, parents, 1994 and 1998 degrees, teaching before politics and 14 October 2008 election. Although the page path and publication label say December 2024, its body has been updated to describe him as former prime minister; do not assign every sentence to that original publication date. Private family details and unrelated allegations were not copied into the dossier.

Read the Commons roles and election tables. Papineau service runs from 14 October 2008 through 27 April 2025, with re-elections in 2011, 2015, 2019 and 2021. The database records premier tenure 4 November 2015–14 March 2025, and Liberal leadership from 15 April 2013 through 8 March 2025. These are role-record conventions, distinct from election events on 14 April 2013 and 9 March 2025. Parliamentary service does not end on the premier resignation day. No claim that he still holds a seat.

Read the relevant party-leaders appendix footnote confirming Trudeau’s election as leader on 14 April 2013 after interim leader Bob Rae. Distinguish that event from the roles table’s 15 April commencement. The appendix concerns party leadership, not a nationwide election to the premiership. The full history of all parties was not reviewed.

Read the Governor General’s captions documenting the 4 November 2015 swearing-in, administration of the oaths, and the 29th Canadian ministry. The prime-minister ordinal is 23rd, not the cabinet ordinal 29th found in scraped labels. Text and metadata were reviewed, not image pixels or the full recording. The 19 October election and 4 November inauguration are separate.

Read the commissioner’s 14 August 2019 release, including the finding under section 9, Trudeau’s stated concern about jobs and economic consequences, the efforts to influence the attorney general, and the explanation that success was not required for a breach. This was the Trudeau II ethics examination, not a criminal conviction of Trudeau and not merely an untested allegation. The commissioner also reported limits on access to Cabinet confidences; no claim of unrestricted access or an independent reinvestigation is made.

Read selected executive-summary passages and testimony excerpts in the original Trudeau II report PDF. Section 9 concerns improper advancement of private interests through influence; the report found that Trudeau sought to influence Jody Wilson-Raybould over whether the prosecution director should invite SNC-Lavalin to remediation-agreement negotiations. His employment rationale is recorded as his position, not proof that the pressure was lawful. No full reading of all 2268 extracted lines, audit of underlying witness files, or later criminal-procedure conclusion is claimed.

Read the implementation statement’s introductory paragraphs: 30 November 2018 signature, 10 December 2019 amendment and 1 July 2020 commencement. Cross-checked actual commencement with Global Affairs Canada’s current Joint Review page, rather than treating the earlier planned date alone as proof of implementation. CUSMA, USMCA, ACEUM and T-MEC are national-language names for the same agreement. No claim of unilateral personal authorship, automatic tariff elimination in every case, or completed 2026 review outcome.

Read Reuters’ September 2021 election report on Investing.com, including the early election, minority government since 2019, failure to gain a majority and need to work with other parties. Its contemporaneous leading-seat figures were still preliminary and are not republished as final totals. The Commons table independently confirms the 20 September vote. Retaining government does not mean winning most popular votes, a separate direct premiership ballot, or a single-party majority.

Read the short Governor General event record for 14 March 2025: Trudeau presented his resignation shortly before Carney’s swearing-in. This actual sequence fixes the resignation day. It is separate from his January announcement, Carney’s March party election and the later end of Trudeau’s parliamentary service. The archive label does not make the described event prospective.

Read Health Canada’s 17 October 2018 release and selected rules. It describes a regulated adult market and continued restrictions, including prohibitions on sale to minors and impaired driving; it is not unrestricted legalization. Government predictions about public-health benefits or criminal profits are not asserted as independently achieved outcomes. Old age limits or possession advice are not offered as current legal guidance.

Read Finance Canada’s March 2025 backgrounder: federal fuel charge and consumer-price requirements cease from 1 April 2025, while industrial carbon pricing continues as a separate policy area. The change occurred after Trudeau left office; do not attribute the cancellation to his earlier government or claim all carbon pricing was abolished. Political descriptions of effectiveness are not independent measurements of emissions reduction.

Read Brown University’s report of the actual 22 September 2026 Ogden Lecture conversation with president Christina Paxson. It identifies Trudeau as former prime minister and describes discussion of Canada–US relations, AI regulation and civic participation, furnishing recent life-status evidence. Unlike the earlier September 9 event advertisement, this reports completed participation. His remarks about trade and US policy are attributed opinions, not independently verified forecasts or official positions of the current Canadian government. No full video or photo pixels inspected.

Read Sadeen Mohsen’s Canadian Press report on CityNews, posted 7 November 2026. It reports Oxford’s Friday announcement, 6 November, of a Distinguished Fellowship and World Leaders Circle membership and quotes Trudeau’s response. This is a secondary account of the school release; the school’s primary biography could not be opened, and the foundation listing’s indexed snippet was not reproduced in its readable body. No professorship, new degree, settled teaching load, exact contractual term or actual Oxford campus appearance is asserted. The September 11 Toronto photo caption is not the November announcement date.

Read the relevant 2015 and 2025 rows and explanatory text of the Commons ministries appendix. It confirms 9 March 2025 Carney party election and 14 March swearing-in upon Trudeau’s resignation. Its table ends Trudeau’s ministry on 13 March, using a succession-boundary convention, while the roles table and Governor General’s account document actual resignation on 14 March. Preserve the latter event date without silently claiming all tables match. Prime ministers and ministries have different ordinals.

Read CRA notice FCN16 background and current-status sections: the Greenhouse Gas Pollution Pricing Act came into force on 21 June 2018, Part 1 covered fuel charges, and Part 2 industrial output-based pricing. The 14 March 2025 announcement preceded rates being set to zero from 1 April; earlier liabilities were not erased. This operational notice is not a full statutory or current individual-tax assessment. Public text distinguishes historical creation, later cessation of fuel charges and continuing industrial system.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified native-language human review. No original birth/degree certificates, complete ethics report or underlying witness file audit, full treaty/legal audit, event recording or portrait pixels inspected. Source titles and present-tense biographies can be stale; preserve distinctions between office dates, announcements, elections, legal findings and attributed opinions. Refresh offices and complete source-specific portrait rights and visual checks before publication.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed against Chinese and English. Preserve 1971 birth, separate 1994 BA and 1998 BEd; 2008 election and April 2025 parliamentary endpoint; April 2013 election versus role commencement; 2015 election versus swearing-in and 23rd premier versus 29th ministry; 2019 section 9 ethics violation versus criminal conviction; 2018 treaty signature, 2019 amendment and 2020 entry into force; 2021 minority versus majority; March 2025 party election versus resignation and parliamentary endpoint; April fuel-charge removal versus industrial pricing; September actual Brown event versus November Oxford announcement. Fellow does not imply professorship. CUSMA/ACEUM/T-MEC translations refer to the same agreement.
